clue.text: Is tale about one who served?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the preceding words are read from the end back

blocks.note: a saga is a long tale

explanation.surface: A question about whether a story is really about someone who did military or domestic service.
explanation.walkthrough: IS followed by SAGA, the whole reversed, gives AGASSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is a former tennis champion, and serving is how every tennis point begins.

clue.text: Vet with aggressive cat delivering first character test

indicators.note: delivering means handing over, so the opening letter is given away

blocks.note: to vet accounts is to audit them
a lion is a fierce big cat

explanation.surface: A vet with a fierce cat issuing a first character assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: LION loses its first letter to give ION. Character test sounds like a personality check, but character means a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An audition is a trial performance used to test an actor or musician.

clue.text: Shy of masculine guy drinking fine, cool cordial

indicators.note: shy of means short of, so a letter is missing
drinking means taking something inside

blocks.note: F for fine, as on pencils
fab is slang for great, cool

explanation.surface: A shy man sipping a fine, chilled fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE without M is ALE, which takes in F plus FAB. Cordial looks like the drink but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and good-natured, the same warmth that cordial describes.

clue.text: Left abandoning Southern congestion charge – could the French set up this route?

indicators.note: abandoning means a letter leaves the word
set up in a down clue means lifted, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: London's Ultra Low Emission Zone charge on drivers

explanation.surface: A London driving charge question: could the French have built this?
explanation.walkthrough: ULEZ is the London charge on polluting cars; removing L leaves UEZ. The French did build the Suez Canal, a waterway joining the Mediterranean and Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suez Canal is a shipping route linking the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

clue.text: Perhaps Google challenger, one going for nothing, will get the thumbs-up …

indicators.note: going for means one thing leaves and another takes its place

blocks.note: Google is an example of an app
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A rival tech firm hoping to win endorsement from users or regulators.
explanation.walkthrough: Google is the example of an app; going for means swapping the one for the nothing inside the challenger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the thumbs-up is the idiomatic gesture of agreement, so it stands for approval.

clue.text: Suggestion of green activity depressing one in eight in Twickenham maybe …

blocks.note: putting is the activity on a golf green

blocks.clueFragment: one in eight in Twickenham maybe
blocks.note: a rugby union pack has eight forwards; Twickenham is England's rugby stadium

explanation.surface: A sporting mix-up: golf on top of a rugby forward at Twickenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Depressing means pressing down on: in this down clue the golf word sits above the rugby word. Twickenham is the London home of English rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting forward an idea is proposing it, so the gerund names a suggestion.

clue.text: … review arising in March/middle of April

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of the following word
arising in a down clue means going upward, reading the letters from the bottom

explanation.surface: A review is held in the spring, sometime between March and April.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE plus R, reversed. March looks like the month but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a short review summarising what has gone before.

clue.text: One who once scored six against German outfit?

blocks.note: Aldi is a German supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A footballer who once scored six against a German team.
explanation.walkthrough: Scored means wrote music, not hit the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivaldi was a Baroque composer, and scoring is writing music for instruments.

clue.text: Refuse meat when middle becomes dry

indicators.note: becomes means one part turns into something else

blocks.note: liver is offal eaten as meat
the central letter of the meat word
TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink

explanation.surface: Turning down meat once its centre is too dry.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVER swaps its middle V for TT. Refuse is the noun, rubbish, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is rubbish dropped carelessly, which is what refuse means as a noun.

clue.text: Doubts views underpinning Spare

blocks.note: a second is a spare or backup

explanation.surface: Doubts about opinions that support Prince Harry's memoir Spare.
explanation.walkthrough: Underpinning in a down clue means the views go below the spare word. Spare is also the title of Prince Harry's memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Having second thoughts means reconsidering, which is to have doubts.

clue.text: … unlike official sport ebbing into recession

indicators.note: ebbing describes a tide flowing back, so the letters run the opposite way
into places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: short for referee, a match official
F1, Formula One motor racing, with the 1 read as I
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, an official sport losing money as the economy shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: REF plus F1 is reversed to IFFER, which goes into DENT. Recession here means a hollow, not an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are unlike each other are different; the adjective swaps cleanly into a sentence.

clue.text: Hunger after former runner eats very thriftily to begin with

indicators.note: something that eats takes another thing inside it
to begin with points to just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: Sebastian Coe, the retired British middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: Hungry after an ex-athlete who eats very frugally from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: COE takes in V, then T is added: COVE plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunger after something is to crave or desire it, which is what covet means.

clue.text: Leaves before old boat sadly takes on volume of water?

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a bad order
takes on means accepts something aboard, holding it inside

blocks.note: cc, cubic centimetres, a measure of liquid volume

explanation.surface: An old boat in poor shape is leaking and shipping water before being abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled BOAT then O, with CC slipped in between. Leaves is a noun here, not someone departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the dried leaves of a plant, prepared for smoking or chewing.

clue.text: Urge mummy's boy to lose weight ahead of posh university

indicators.note: to lose means a letter is dropped from the word before

blocks.note: a mummy's boy is a weakling

explanation.surface: An instruction for a pampered son to slim down before going to an elite university.
explanation.walkthrough: WIMP loses its W to leave IMP. U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge to act, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Aussie finally opening tinny having put love before the drink

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word beside it
opening means prising something apart, with a letter going into the gap

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
tinny is Australian slang for a can of beer

explanation.surface: An Australian cracking open a can of beer after declaring love for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinny is Australian slang for a beer can. The drink looks like the beer but is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal slang for the sea, as in falling into the drink.

clue.text: Opinionated note put in computer by setter?

indicators.note: put in means placed inside another word

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A setter types a dogmatic note into their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter looks like the crossword compiler, but here it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dogmatic insists their views are right, which is what opinionated describes.

clue.text: Imprisoning wrong 'un, a right mouthful for judge

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking something inside

blocks.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

explanation.surface: A judge gives a jailed villain a right telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A mouthful sounds like a scolding, but it is a bite of food, split after its third letter to take the villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute between two parties.

clue.text: Understand kids, right?

explanation.surface: A parent asking whether they understand children properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Kids is a verb (fools), not children.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret or understand a statement in a particular way.

clue.text: Band together with husband cutting most of volume for song and dance

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is left off
cutting means slicing into another word and sitting inside it

blocks.note: to band together is to ally

explanation.surface: A musical group and a husband taking part in a song and dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: Band together looks like a group name but is a verb meaning unite.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is an idiom for a fuss, and ballyhoo is noisy fuss or hype.

clue.text: Generally when beer drinking regret finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early means the word stops short of its final letter
drinking means taking something inside

explanation.surface: Usually, beer drinking leads to regret if you stop early.
explanation.walkthrough: When stands for as, the sense of 'as I left' meaning 'when I left'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a rule is an idiom meaning usually or generally.

clue.text: Cereal bar name half promises to be good for you

indicators.note: bar here means except, so the following thing is excluded
half means only the first half of the next word is used

blocks.note: the first two of four letters of VOWS

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal bar whose name claims it will be healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cereal bar reads like a snack, but bar means without: BRAN without N, then half of VOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Good for you is an exclamation of praise, and bravo is a cheer of approval.

clue.text: On the ball, turnover of Dundee's wingers alarmed

indicators.note: wingers are on the flanks, so only the outside letters are kept
turnover means flipping the order of those letters

explanation.surface: A football report about a team losing possession of Dundee's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnover sounds like losing the ball in sport but here flips letters. Dundee is a Scottish city with two football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerted means warned, and to be alarmed is to be warned of danger.

clue.text: Small winnings making United mania ultimately thin on the ground

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before
making here means one letter is turned into another

blocks.note: abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: Small prize money makes the excitement around Manchester United scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: PURSE swaps its U for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means scattered and scanty, which is an idiom of things being thin on the ground.

clue.text: Father quaffing large brew back in bijou flat

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking, so something is swallowed inside
back in points to the end letter of the next word

blocks.note: pa is an informal name for a father
a brew is a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Dad drinking a large mug of tea in the back of a tiny apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat looks like an apartment, but it is a stretch of level land.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high, level ground, so flat names it as a noun.

clue.text: Bored by Hello and so on's set of moral values

indicators.note: a word bored by another has a hole drilled into it and gets filled

blocks.note: etc. abbreviates et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Someone bored by Hello magazine and the like and its moral codes.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello reads like the celebrity magazine; it is just the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a principle or body of moral principles guiding conduct.

clue.text: Foolish spectator swapping ends in Luton

indicators.note: swapping means one letter is exchanged for another

blocks.note: Luton ends in L and N; the N in the spectator word becomes L

explanation.surface: A silly football fan at a Luton match.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of Luton are L and N; WITNESS changes its N to L.
explanation.definitionFit: Witless means lacking wit or sense, which is a synonym for foolish.

clue.text: Heard neckwear's uncomfortable?

indicators.note: heard means we go by how a word is pronounced rather than written

blocks.note: a ruff is a stiff pleated collar

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a collar is itchy.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruff is the frilled Elizabethan collar; the answer is spelt differently but pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling rough is British idiom for feeling unwell or uncomfortable.

clue.text: Hot before, in the past, later and in the future

blocks.note: abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A jumble of time words: before, past, later, future.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter is an adverb meaning from now on, at a later time.

clue.text: Concern of former royal having stopped duty

indicators.note: something that has stopped a word plugs it, sitting in the middle

blocks.note: excise is a tax or duty

explanation.surface: Worry about an ex-royal who has given up their duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Former looks like it gives the ex at the front, but that already sits in the duty word; former only marks the royal as the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise someone is to worry or concern them, as in being exercised about an issue.

clue.text: Put your oar in sea and paddle home wiped out

indicators.note: wiped out means removed entirely from the word

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a home

explanation.surface: Rowing at sea, with the oars and paddling, until the household is swept away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pad is informal for a flat or home; the Med is the usual crossword sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your oar in is an idiom for interfering, which is what meddling is.
